title: Deep muscles of the pectoral region and axilla (anterior)
lab: Anterior Thorax, Axilla, and Anterior Arm
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender, with surface detail added by an image model.

rows: Ribs 3 to 5, near their costal cartilages.
Pulls the scapula forward and down and holds it against the chest wall.
hy: Divides the axillary artery into its three parts: the first part is medial to it, the second behind it, and the third lateral to it.

rows: Outer surfaces of the upper eight or nine ribs.
Anterior surface of the medial border of the scapula.
Protracts the scapula and holds it against the chest wall. Rotates the scapula upward so that the arm can be raised above the head.
hy: Injury to the long thoracic nerve (for example in axillary lymph node dissection) causes a winged scapula and difficulty raising the arm above the horizontal.

rows: Tip of the coracoid process of the scapula.
Middle third of the medial surface of the humerus.
Flexes and adducts the arm at the shoulder.
hy: The musculocutaneous nerve pierces this muscle on its way into the arm.

structures.name: Short head of biceps brachii muscle
prompts: Short head of biceps brachii muscle

rows: Tip of the coracoid process of the scapula.
Radial tuberosity and, through the bicipital aponeurosis, the deep fascia of the forearm.
Supinates the forearm and flexes the elbow. Helps flex the arm at the shoulder.

structures.name: Long head of biceps brachii muscle
prompts: Long head of biceps brachii muscle

rows: Supraglenoid tubercle of the scapula. Its tendon runs through the shoulder joint and down the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus.
Radial tuberosity and, through the bicipital aponeurosis, the deep fascia of the forearm.
Supinates the forearm and flexes the elbow. Its tendon helps hold the head of the humerus in the glenoid cavity.
hy: Rupture of the long head tendon lets the belly bunch up in the distal part of the arm, just above the elbow (Popeye deformity).

rows: Junction of the first rib and its costal cartilage.
Groove on the lower surface of the middle third of the clavicle.
Anchors and depresses the clavicle, steadying it at the sternoclavicular joint during movements of the shoulder.
Subscapular fossa on the anterior surface of the scapula.
Upper and lower subscapular nerves (C5, C6).
Medially rotates the arm. With the other rotator cuff muscles it holds the head of the humerus in the glenoid cavity.
Spinous processes of T7 to T12, thoracolumbar fascia, iliac crest, and the lower three or four ribs.
Floor of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus.
Extends, adducts, and medially rotates the arm.
hy: A lady between two majors: latissimus dorsi inserts in the floor of the intertubercular sulcus, between pectoralis major on the lateral lip and teres major on the medial lip.

rows: Posterior surface of the inferior angle of the scapula.
Medial lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus.
Adducts and medially rotates the arm. Helps extend it from a flexed position.
Distal half of the anterior surface of the humerus.
Coronoid process and tuberosity of the ulna.
Musculocutaneous nerve (C5, C6). A small lateral part is supplied by the radial nerve.
Flexes the elbow in every position of the forearm.
Long head: infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula. Lateral head: posterior humerus above the radial groove. Medial head: posterior humerus below the radial groove.
Extends the elbow. The long head helps extend and adduct the arm at the shoulder.
hy: The triceps reflex tests mainly C7.
